acceptance.given: An evaluation request supplies a target not supported by the toolchain target policy.

oracle.expected: The target-evaluation implementation rejects the request with a non-success outcome and records the unsupported-target reason.
forbidden: A successful evaluation result is returned for the unsupported target.
The implementation inspects or continues processing the unsupported target as valid.
oracle.observable: Runtime result emitted by the target-evaluation path, including terminal status and rejection reason.

acceptance.then: During target evaluation, before inspection or execution proceeds.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the target-evaluation test with an unsupported target and assert that it fails closed without a successful result.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Bind target evaluation to the supported-target policy so unsupported targets are rejected before inspection, and preserve a runtime assertion for the rejection outcome.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No persisted schema or state change; rollback restores prior target-policy handling.

slice_hint.state_transition: unsupported target request -> rejected terminal result
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Evaluation terminates with an unsupported-target rejection and no success verdict.

acceptance.given: A matrix evidence set contains an infrastructure-failed case or infrastructure failure marker.

oracle.expected: The matrix evidence aggregator marks the aggregate invalid and refuses to emit a valid aggregate verdict.
forbidden: Infrastructure-failed matrix evidence is included in a valid aggregate.
The aggregator reports success while any required evidence is infrastructure-failed.
oracle.observable: Aggregate result object and its validity/terminal verdict fields after aggregation.

acceptance.then: When evaluating and aggregating matrix evidence.
acceptance.when: The matrix evidence is affected by infrastructure failure.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Feed the aggregator a matrix case carrying an infrastructure-failure status and assert that aggregate validity is rejected.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Ensure aggregate validity computation treats infrastructure-failed evidence as invalid and propagates that terminal state.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No state or schema migration; rollback only reverts aggregate validity logic.

slice_hint.state_transition: matrix evidence with infrastructure failure -> invalid aggregate
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Aggregate result is invalid whenever any required matrix evidence is infrastructure-failed.

acceptance.given: Production entry points and frozen test snapshots are declared as separate artifact sets.

oracle.expected: A boundary validation proves every declared production owner is outside the frozen test snapshot set.
forbidden: A production owner path appears in a frozen test snapshot.
The boundary is accepted solely because files exist without checking path membership.
oracle.observable: Deterministic ownership-boundary validation output listing production owners and snapshot paths with an explicit disjointness result.

acceptance.then: During snapshot freezing and ownership-boundary validation.
acceptance.when: Production owners are checked against frozen test snapshots.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the ownership-boundary validator against a snapshot containing a declared production owner and assert deterministic failure.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Enforce disjoint production-owner and frozen-test-snapshot path sets and expose a machine-checkable boundary result.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No persisted data change; rollback removes only the boundary validation enforcement.

slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Validation passes only when no production-owner path is contained in frozen test snapshots.

acceptance.given: The repository lists existing fixtures under S2, S7, and S24 for specific declared roles.

oracle.expected: Verification evidence records each listed fixture's declared role and demonstrates behavior through executed assertions; role mismatches or existence-only evidence are rejected.
forbidden: Fixture existence alone is reported as behavioral proof.
A listed fixture is assigned or used for an undeclared role.
oracle.observable: Per-fixture verification records containing role identity, executed assertion outcomes, and rejection of existence-only evidence.

acceptance.then: When retaining and evaluating the listed S2, S7, and S24 fixtures.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Execute fixture verification with an existence-only record or an undeclared role and assert that the verifier rejects it.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Record and validate declared roles for S2/S7/S24 fixtures while requiring executed behavioral assertions instead of file-presence checks.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Evidence record format remains backward-compatible; rollback restores prior role/assertion validation.

slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Every listed fixture has a matching declared role and at least one executed behavior assertion; otherwise verification fails.
